1. By this order I shall decide the revision petition filed by the revisionist under Section 397 of Cr.P.C challenging the impugned order dated 08.07.2022, passed by the Ld. MM South, Saket Courts,
Delhi in case titled as "State Vs. Sarabjeet Singh & Ors." whereby the Ld. Trial court has declared revisionist as absconder.

2. Brief facts relevant and necessary for deciding the present revision petition are that the FIR No.
46/2018 u/s 498A/406/377/506/323/34 IPC was registered against the Digitally signed by revisionist/ accused at PS Hauz Khas, Delhi.

During the PURSHOTTAM PURSHOTTAM PATHAK PATHAK Date: investigation, the investigating officer moved an 2024.07.12 16:07:45 +0530 application for issuance of NBW against the revisionist as Gaurav Singh Vs. State and Anr.
he was not joining the investigation.

sentences.text: On 07.02.2022, Ld. MM, South, Saket issued NBW against the revisionist which remained unexecuted.
Thereafter, on 04.04.2022, investigating officer moved an application before Ld. Trial Court requesting to issue proclamation u/s 82 Cr.P.C.,which was returnable for 31.05.2022.

On 31.05.2022 an application for stay of proceedings u/s 82 Cr.P.c was moved by the counsel for the revisionist, in which the counsel for revisionist averred that the notice was never served upon him and therefore, the proceedings are not tenable and liable to the stayed.
The said application was dismissed and on same day notice was issued to the process server for recording of his statement.
The revisionist did not challenge this order.
After recording the statement of process server, the Ld. Trial Court declared the accused absconder on 08.07.2022.
Thus, the revisionist/ accused has challenged the order dated 08.07.2022, declaring him as a proclaimed offender.

sentences.text: 3. I have heard arguments advanced by Ld. counsel for revisionist and Ld. Addl. PP for the State.

4. Ld. Counsel for the revisionist has argued that the impugned order dated 08.07.2022 is not sustainable in law as the revisionist/accused was declared proclaimed offender without considering the facts and circumstances of the case.

He further argued that from the material Digitally signed by PURSHOTTAM PURSHOTTAM PATHAK PATHAK available on record, it is clear that the revisionist / accused Date:
2024.07.12 16:07:54 +0530 was not aware about the registration of any FIR against him, hence, he was not concealing himself or absconding Gaurav Singh Vs. State and Anr.
at the time when he was declared absconder.

sentences.text: Thus, the order of Ld. Trial Court declaring him as a proclaimed offender shall be set-aside.
5. It appears from the perusal of record that in the present case, the FIR was registered on 18.02.2018.
Ld. Counsel for the revisionist has contended that the revisionist was out of India from the date of registration of FIR till the date when he was declared as absconder i.e. 08.07.2022.

He has submitted that the revisionist came to know about the adverse order at a later stage when during court proceedings his mother was informed that revisionist has been declared proclaimed offender.

In support of his contention that the revisionist was not in India at the said time, he has filed two air tickets, one dated 14.09.2019 from Delhi to Aukland and another dated 14.10.2023 from Aukland to Toronto.
However, Ld. Counsel failed to explain how on the basis of these two travel tickets his claim that revisionist was out of India for the said period can be accepted.
He has not filed any document pertaining to the course which revisionist was pursuing in Aukland.
He has also not filed the copy of passport and air tickets showing how many times he traveled between India to Aukland and duration of his stay in both the countries.
6. Even if it is believed that he left India on 14.09.2019, prior to that notice u/s 41 A Cr.P.C. was PURSHOTTAM already served to him on 18.02.2018.
There is also no PATHAK force in the contention of Ld. Counsel that revisionist was PATHAK not concealing himself.

Perusal of record shows that Gaurav Singh Vs. State and Anr.
notices u/s 41A Cr.P.C., were issued to the revisionist on 18.02.2018, 21.12.2021 and 14.01.2022 which were received by the mother of accused and only when the revisionist did not respond to these notices, NBWs were issued against him.

sentences.text: The revisionist was well aware about the proceedings against him in the said FIR and instead of submitting himself to jurisdiction of Ld. Trial Court the revisionist has been trying to subvert the cause of justice by filing the present revision petition.
The conduct of revisionist has been contumacious in not joining the investigation and to avoid proceeding despite being aware of it.
Hence, I do not find any reason to set-aside the impugned order passed by Ld. Trial Court.
7. Along with the revision petition an application for condonation of delay has also been filed by the revisionist.

sentences.text: The revisionist took about 2 years to file the revision petition.
The grounds taken by the revisionist for seeking the condonation of delay in filing the present revision petition is not tenable at all.
The application moved u/s 5 of Limitation Act is therefore rejected.
9. Hence, the revision petition being devoid of any merit and also to have been filed beyond period of limitation is dismissed.
10. TCR be sent back to the Ld. Trial court along with copy of judgment.
11. Revision petition be consigned to record room after due compliance.
